transcript.speaker: Finnegan O'Malley
transcript.content: Imelda, I want you to have a chance to mend things with your father, and I care enough to support that, but I'm genuinely worried about meeting him because of the racist and emotionally manipulative behaviour you've told me about. If we do meet, I'd need clear boundaries — a public place, a short time limit, agreed topics to avoid, and a signal so I can leave if it becomes toxic. If that feels impossible, I'm happy to support you in other ways: I can come with you to a counselling session, or wait nearby while you see him and check in afterward. Which of those options would make you feel safest?
